- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day) and sentiment is neutral or negative, cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to correct — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day of lag.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid false optimism.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility — apply smoothing: if last 3–5 days show high variance, reduce forecast volatility by 10–20%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend, but not exceed 3% above recent high.
